messages:
lina: RFC follow-up: proposing tenant opt-in for compatibility shims rather than flipping a global flag. quick sync?

sam: yeah, sounds safer. do you mean per-tenant metadata + gateway header or client-provided header?

lina: per-tenant metadata in control plane. gateway injects header so clients don't need changes.

ben: thinking about cache fragmentation: if we change request shape (tokenization/embeddings dims), runtime cache keys diverge.

maria: agree. primary risk is KV cache hit rate drop. we need metrics up-front to decide.

sam: possible mitigation: include compat_version in cache key so behavior is explicit. tradeoff is more entries.

lina: proposed short-term: control-plane opt-in + include compat tag in cache keys. long-term: consider edge translation that normalizes payloads before runtime.

ben: ops concern: doubling cache entries for even a few tenants can increase GPU mem pressure. prefer doing translation at the gateway/sidecar to preserve runtime cache.

maria: gateway sidecar reduces backend cost but adds p95 at edge and complicates ordering for rollout (gateway -> runtime dependency).

sam: TL;DR tradeoffs: control-plane toggle + in-runtime shim = simpler orchestration, higher backend memory/ps cost. gateway translation = lower backend cost, higher per-request latency and routing complexity.

arch-bot: suggestion: emit telemetry tag "compat.opt_in" and record cache_hit_rate_by_compat, tokens_per_req_delta, and p95_by_compat_version during canary.

lina: add to checklist: audit log entry when control plane toggles a tenant (enterprise compliance). also add prune policy for expirations.

ops-bot: recommend autoscaling guard while canary runs. if cache miss spike causes CPU/GPU spillover, scale earlier.

ben: timeline: implement control-plane field + cache-key tag. run 2-week canary on 4 tenants with mixed traffic profiles. if cache hit falls > 20% or mem > 15% then pivot to gateway translation for those tenants.

maria: +1. i'll build dashboards: cache_hit_rate_by_compat, p95_tail_by_compat, tpr_delta. will add alerts: cache hit delta > 15% OR p95 increase > 50ms.

sam: control-plane schema note: add tenant.compat_opt_in: version (string), expires_at (ISO). gateway reads and appends header X-RW-Compat. implement auth checks so only org-admins can toggle.

lina: example control-plane patch: ```json
{"tenant_id":"t-99","compat_opt_in":"v3.0","expires_at":"2026-09-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

lina: example curl to simulate flow: ```bash
curl -H "X-RW-Compat: v3.0" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

arch-bot: also: schedule automated prune job: remove compat tags after expires_at + 30d and emit metric deprecation.pruned.

ben: action items: ben -> cost + mem impact estimate for doubling cache keys on sample QPS (will post numbers tomorrow); sam -> PR for control-plane schema + RBAC; maria -> dashboards + alerts; lina -> gateway header read + propagate + RFC draft for long-term edge translation option.

sam: i'll PR schema today and add migration testing.

maria: will stub dashboards and mock data so we can validate alerts before canary.

lina: aim to start canary next Tue. keep this lightweight and reversible. i'll write short RFC note capturing edge-translation fallback and deprecation pruning policy. :thumbsup:

arch-bot: reminder: add opt-in audit events to retention matrix and tag for SOC review."
